variants.headline: A company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen the failure of {company}.
variants.body:
The company {company} has gone under. The failure is a business event, not a detailed account of its consequences for particular people. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known outcome from unreported claims about creditors, employment or the circumstances that brought the company to this position.

Our principles ask how an economy serves the colony, including when an enterprise fails. A business outcome should not make the people around it disappear into a convenient political slogan. Responsibility deserves an argument about stewardship, rather than a ready-made morality tale built from facts that are not known.

The responsibility of {target} should be examined without presuming the failure's cause. This paper records the business outcome while leaving unreported financial, employment and legal particulars outside its factual account. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.
